items.summary: Asian stocks wobbled on Nov 12 as Nvidia shares plunged more than 8% after the bell, weighing on S&P 500 e-mini futures that slipped 0.4%. The board is meeting late on Nov 11 to decide whether to oust chief executive Jensen Huang amid allegations he had an affair with a suspected spy for China and another company executive. Regional indexes fared better; South Korea’s Kospi rose 0.2%, Taiwanese shares gained 0.5% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed 0.5%. Fed funds futures price an 87.3% chance of a 25-basis-point hike on Dec 9, per CME Group’s FedWatch.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Ousting Jensen Huang Amid Stock Slide

items.summary: A Thursday briefing newsletter explores what is known about the relationship between Jensen Huang, founder of Nvidia, and Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed. The New York Times reported that US intelligence believes Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese services to spy for Beijing, though the underlying evidence remains classified. Nvidia said her interactions were “not unusual or unexpected”, while she admitted in a letter to employees that he had been unfaithful and described himself as “deeply sorry”. Nvidia’s share price fell sharply after reports its board considered ousting him. The newsletter notes speculation about whether Alice Huang could have gained access to US AI policy through her husband, but calls it unfounded without evidence. Experts suggest the Chinese agency MSS may have used a romantic relationship as a recruitment method, though China denies any involvement.
items.title: Newsletter examines Nvidia affair and Alice Huang espionage claims

items.summary: MIT researchers developed a training method that produces faster and more adaptable artificial intelligence models for climate prediction, known as climate emulators. The approach generates optimized synthetic data so an emulator can be trained by running one full earth system model instead of six or eight times, cutting production time from months to seconds. Christoher Womack says the technique lets scientists explore future scenarios more reliably and trust their outputs for policy decisions. Noelle Selin adds that updating tools will help researchers and practitioners in the long run.
items.title: MIT technique speeds climate AI models

items.summary: A publication frames a possible leadership change at Nvidia as unlikely but imminent, citing Kalshi odds that Jensen Huang survives the week at 30%. It notes no succession plan exists and lists candidates: Lisa Su of AMD; Eric Schmidt, who ran Google from 2001 to 2011 and chaired the National Security Commission on AI from 2018 to 2021; Intel’s Lip-Bu Tan, whose company reported third-quarter revenue up 21% to $16.5 billion before warning of a weak fourth quarter that sent its stock down 20% in after-hours trading and more than 30% since September; Bret Taylor; Ian Buck, an Nvidia vice president who helped develop CUDA; Andrew Bell, with the company for 25 years as of this writing; and Lori Huang. The piece calls itself a parlor game while speculation continues.
items.title: Speculating on Nvidia’s Possible CEO Successors Amid Jensen Huang Scandal

items.summary: The Indonesian rupiah fell to an all-time low of 18,241 per US dollar on Nov 12 (quantity-812-818), its worst performance in 2026. Bank Indonesia intervened across offshore and domestic forwards plus spot markets and government bond purchases to stabilise it (entity-504-518). Pressure stems from a stronger dollar, MSCI reclassification risk, fragile investor sentiment and political uncertainty after Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka’s resignation.
items.title: Bank Indonesia Intervenes as Rupiah Hits Record Low

items.summary: The New York Times reports that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang is suspected of a second extramarital affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia vice president. The outlet says it was told by five employees and cites video showing the two at a San Jose hotel during a conference earlier this year. Both are married. Nvidia has rules against such relationships, its board is investigating his admitted affair, and House Republicans say Congress may subpoena him over spy allegations.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang accused of second affair

items.summary: At Data + AI Summit, Databricks announced the general availability of Genie Ontology, a layer that provides enterprise business context to AI agents. The release adds new sources for agents to learn from and tools for people to curate knowledge, including generally available features such as Domains and subdomains, Unity Catalog Pages, Organizational directories starting with Workday, and Ontology Snippets. Databricks also expanded Genie Search's supported systems to Google Drive, Jira, Confluence and Workday, with SharePoint in beta. A benchmark developed with Turing compared Genie against two frontier agents on a simulated UK energy supplier workspace; the results were not independently verified by Databricks. According to that benchmark, Genie answered correctly in 91% of runs, performed at 1.6 times the rate of the stronger frontier agent, used less than half the tokens and finished three to four times faster. Customers including Virgin Atlantic, Agrifirm and BHG Financial provided testimonials about improved accuracy and speed.
items.title: Databricks Announces General Availability of Genie Ontology

items.summary: Databricks announced updates to its Genie Agents, which help teams turn business questions into actionable insights grounded in enterprise context. The agents now analyze unstructured documents within Unity Catalog volumes, connect to tools via native MCP connectors, and can be shared externally through OpenSharing or privately through Genie Clean Rooms. Databricks claims 80% of the context that runs an enterprise lives in documents such as contracts and reports (quantity-1901-1904). Vinodh Simon of Verana Health said his team plans to use Genie Agents for unstructured clinical data, while Slack's Jaime DeLanghe praised bringing governed insights into workflows. Unstructured analysis is in Public Preview; MCP connectors are generally available; OpenSharing and Genie Clean Rooms remain in beta.
items.title: Databricks Unveils Genie Agents Updates for Data Analysis and Sharing

items.summary: On Nov. 12, the case brought by two Ethiopian nationals and the Katiba Institute against Meta will return to the Kenya High Court after a ruling that Facebook's Nairobi content review center gave Kenyan courts jurisdiction. The petitioners allege Meta's algorithms amplified hateful content during the Tigray war between 2020 and 2022, which preceded the murder of one petitioner’s father in November 2021. Meta argued it could not be subject to Kenyan law as an unregistered company. The article notes Kenya's youth unemployment stands at 67%, a factor cited for government support of Meta-linked firms.
items.title: Meta Returns to Kenya’s High Court Over Hate Speech in Ethiopia

items.summary: The Australian government has warned employers that artificial intelligence could bring either fewer hours and higher wages or greater burnout and surveillance for workers, with entry-level roles most exposed. Workplace relations minister Amanda Rishworth launched a best-practice guide urging firms to consult staff on automation’s impact. The Reserve Bank reported little evidence yet of AI disrupting the labour market but flagged high uncertainty about future effects. Opposition figures criticised the approach as voluntary guidance while companies such as Qantas, National Australian Bank and Canva cut thousands of jobs linked partly to AI.
items.title: Australia warns employers of AI job and wage effects

items.summary: The Australian government cancelled its search for a National Solar Panel Recycling Pilot administrator on 10 November, citing undisclosed changes to the industry since April’s tender release. The pilot would have engaged a supplier to collect up to 250,000 decommissioned panels from around 100 sites and recycle them safely.
items.title: Australia Cancels Solar Panel Recycling Pilot

items.summary: Crude oil prices declined as traders weighed hopes for peace in Ukraine and Iran ahead of a US-China summit, with Brent at $91.32 per barrel and WTI at $85.32 (quantity-227-233, quantity-297-303). Reports of higher OPEC production and rising US inventories added downward pressure, though Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks limited losses.
items.title: Oil Prices Fall on Ukraine-Iran Peace Hopes

items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over the failure to blacklist Nvidia customer Megaspeed, accused of illegally diverting advanced US chips to China. According to an Axios report citing sources, at a White House Situation Room meeting after the midterm elections, Bessent questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Entity List. Lutnick initially struggled before saying he would look into it.
items.title: Bessent Presses Lutnick Over Megaspeed Chip Diversion

items.summary: Analysts say Anthropic's share price in its first weeks will be driven more by forced index buying than genuine demand. The firm plans to raise up to $64.4 billion selling 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78, valuing it at up to $1.4 trillion. Like SpaceX, Anthropic is expected to enter six major indexes within five to 15 days of listing. Carsten Hesse of Berenberg said the two deals share similar index-related drivers over those first 15 days. Intropic estimates passive demand will cover about 28 per cent of shares offered, roughly $19 billion. SpaceX's shares rose 50 per cent by day three at $150 a share versus its $135 IPO price. Analysts expect similar early buying for Anthropic.
items.title: Anthropic IPO may follow SpaceX's passive-demand playbook

items.summary: Analysts and investors see Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress as the likely interim CEO while engineer Ian Buck is favoured for a permanent role, following reports of two extramarical affairs involving CEO Jensen Huang. A source familiar with the matter told Reuters that Nvidia's board was meeting Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang, who has overseen the company into becoming the world's second-most valuable firm after a US$600 billion share selloff this week. Prediction market Polymarket showed an 83 per cent chance Huang would resign or be removed by year-end.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Successor Amid Leadership Scandal

items.summary: The Nvidia board is preparing to oust CEO and founder Jensen Huang as soon as Wednesday, according to people familiar with the matter, after media reports detailed a second extramarital affair. The full board has yet to decide; directors are scheduled to meet Wednesday evening. Nvidia’s stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading.
items.title: Nvidia Board Prepares to Oust Jensen Huang

items.summary: Chinese AI companies worry that the Jensen Huang espionage dispute could push the US toward tighter export controls, so they are booking advanced Nvidia chip capacity abroad. Reuters reports firms fear a proposed Remote Access Security Act (RASA) bill may block overseas use of foreign-sourced chips.
items.title: China AI firms scramble for Nvidia chips amid US clampdown

items.summary: A study of Brazil's Bolsa Família cash transfer finds it raises women's formal employment, driven by mothers enrolling young children in school and relaxing care constraints. The effect is larger where local education services are better funded, suggesting public goods complement the transfer.
items.title: Brazil Cash Transfers Boost Women's Employment via School Enrollment

items.summary: The Nvidia board was moving toward removing CEO Jensen Huang over two extramarital affairs, according to The Wall Street Journal. No clear successor exists, per The New York Times. Huang apologized in a message to employees Sunday for being unfaithful. The board announced an independent investigation overseen by former acting U.S. Attorney Joon H. Kim and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz Tuesday, saying it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. China denied espionage claims against Alice Huang.
items.title: Nvidia Board Considers Removing Jensen Huang Amid Affairs and Espionage Claims

items.summary: Nvidia’s board met Wednesday to decide whether to remove CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, following a week in which the company admitted his affair with Alice Huang. After Sunday losses of more than 8% and an estimated $600bn fall in market value since the investigation began, Armina Rosenberg of Minotaur Capital said “the market is starting to price Nvidia without its founder.” Under bylaws Huang can be removed “with or without cause” by a majority vote. The board appointed Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate; Trump and Elon Musk backed him while Warren and Coons urged the administration to preserve export records.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Ousting Jensen Huang Amid Stock Plunge

items.summary: Reports say Nvidia's board is preparing to meet about ousting CEO Jensen Huang amid accusations of a second extramarital affair. The Wall Street Journal, quoting people close to the matter, said the board was preparing to come up with a decision. The New York Times reported video evidence showing Huang being affectionate with vice president Kimberly Powell at a hotel in San Jose, California. Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into reporting that Huang faced a foreign intelligence effort.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Ousting Jensen Huang Over Second Affair

items.summary: Reports of an espionage probe and a second alleged affair have intensified scrutiny of Nvidia's leadership. Shares fell about 8 per cent after-hours, reaching 33 per cent below their early October peak. Analyst Dan Ives told Reuters that 'Jensen is not replaceable … there is no other person on the management team bench.' Huang has led since founding 33 years ago.
items.title: Nvidia Has No Successor Plan Amid Jensen Huang Pressure

items.summary: Chinese leader Xi Jinping is hosting U.S. President Donald Trump for their third summit of the year in Shenzhen, but spy allegations against Nvidia's Jensen Huang are reopening tensions ahead of the meetings. The accusations could give Washington lawmakers grounds to tighten export controls on semiconductors just days before a major leaders' summit. At stake is a yearlong trade truce between top economies that expires in January.
items.title: Xi Welcomes Trump as Nvidia Spy Allegations Strain Trade Truce

items.summary: The Japan Fair Trade Commission approved a business improvement plan from Amazon Japan easing seller pricing rules after an investigation into alleged price-pressure tactics on its e-commerce site. The JFTC will monitor the plan for five years without making a violation finding.
items.title: JFTC Approves Amazon Japan Pricing Plan

items.summary: On Thursday China held a gathering in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth, per Xinhua. Chinese President Xi Jinping addressed attendees; also present were Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi and Ding Xuexiang. The event recalled how more than a century ago Sun led the Revolution of 1911 to abolish China's absolute monarchy.
items.title: China Marks Sun Yat-sen's Birth Anniversary

items.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit a building housing Nasser Hospital's surgical and intensive care wards in southern Gaza, killing at least five Palestinians, including reportedly a surgeon. The Hamas-run Civil Defence agency reported the death toll of 20 people injured. Israel says it targeted militants using medical infrastructure as a command center.
items.title: Israeli Strike on Gaza Hospital Kills at Least Five

items.summary: A BBC report describes how Russia's intensified attacks on Ukraine's energy grid are pushing power supplies close to critical, leaving families in Kyiv facing outages of up to 20 hours. Daryna Kulchytska, a single parent, recounts unreliable rolling blackouts that have been in place since October and are lasting longer than last winter. The article shows the damage at one large power station destroyed by a ballistic missile strike, with recovery hampered by air raids every 15-30 minutes. President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine still has enough generating capacity but struggles to deliver it home; Maxim Timchenko of DTEK warns attacks have doubled in scale and rebuilding will take until next summer.
items.title: Ukraine's Power Grid Near Collapse as Russian Strikes Intensify

items.summary: Michael Lee from the Republic of Korea came to China in 2003, and more than two decades later he now calls Quanzhou in Fujian Province his home. In Jinjiang, a county-level city under Quanzhou and one of China's leading footwear manufacturing hubs, he found a world-class supply chain, constant innovation, and the opportunity to build his own business. His next big plan is to become a true local.
items.title: ROK Entrepreneur Roots His Business in China's Shoe Capital

items.summary: Hundreds of thousands took to the streets across Spain on Wednesday for its first general strike in 14 years, protesting a housing crisis and low wages. Estimates of turnout varied widely between organisers and authorities; Madrid police counted 120,000 against an organiser's half million claim (quantity-1210-1217). More than 70 people were arrested nationwide amid clashes with riot police (quantity-86-95), while unions reported high participation in ports and industry. Unions called it a success; employers dismissed it as a failure.
items.title: Spain's First General Strike in 14 Years Draws Mass Protests

items.summary: Premier David Crisafulli officially reopened the New Burton Coal Mine in Queensland's Bowen Basin, employing 275 workers after receivership in 2025. Owner Argo Resources Queensland said coal royalties did not deter investment and declined to comment on previous owners' losses. CEO Richard Livingstone-Blevins planned to mine 10 million tonnes by 2028.
items.title: Queensland Reopens Coal Mine After Royalty Concerns

items.summary: Zhao Jiyou of the Latin America Branch of China Railway No. 10 Engineering Co., Ltd. describes infrastructure projects across three countries as part of a CGTN series with SASAC on state-owned enterprises in Asia-Pacific connectivity. The group is reinforcing a roadbed in Piura, Peru's northwestern region; it completed rehabilitation of mountain roads at an altitude of 4,500 meters and built the Santiago Apóstol Hospital in Utcubamba with UNOPS support. In Chile, its earlier railway work earned EFE awards. Zhao Jiyou says building connectivity requires both physical infrastructure and closer people-to-people ties.
items.title: China Railway Group Details Peru and Chile Infrastructure Work

items.summary: On Thursday, Israeli occupiers attacked the West Bank town of Atara under army protection, assaulting residents and damaging vehicles while leaving several Palestinians injured, local sources said. Clashes prompted the army to enter the town and fire tear gas canisters, stun grenades and live ammunition. Around 750,000 settlers occupy settlements across the region.
items.title: Israeli forces attack Palestinian town of Atara

items.summary: This morning briefing summarizes several Thursday news items. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, per Russian media (s1). Kirill Dmitriev met them at Vnukovo Airport (s2). Israel's security cabinet ordered military preparations for a possible attack on Iran, reported by KAN (s6), which warned the directives could trigger war (s7); they followed Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot's statement urging Netanyahu to refrain from operations until after Oct. 27 elections (s8-s10). Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan emphasized leaving a cleaner world for future generations at COP31 in Türkiye (s12-s14). FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem said Formula One races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will proceed as scheduled despite Middle East tensions (s17).
items.title: Morning Briefing Covers Russia Talks and Global News

items.summary: The Global wildlife trade regulator CITES has lifted sanctions imposed on Laos in 2023 for failing to control criminal networks trading illegal wildlife products. Laos will now be able to trade in CITES-listed animals without special restriction, but remains under ongoing monitoring. Some conservationists called the move “premature,” arguing that Laos must do more to curb the illegal wildlife trade, which is estimated to be worth billions of dollars a year globally. In 2025, a joint Mongabay investigation with NGO GI-TOC identified 35 illegal wildlife shopping sites in Vientiane and Luang Prabang selling ivory, rhino horn, pangolin scales and other products. By July 2026 the number had grown before most shops closed by August 2026. Authorities reportedly inspected 25 shops, ordered six to close and detained 27 foreign nationals.
items.title: CITES Lifts Sanctions on Laos Amid Conservation Concerns

items.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s opposition has condemned a new law enacted by President Félix Tshisekedi that opens the door to constitutional changes, accusing him of seeking to extend his power. Jean-Baptiste Kasekwa said Tshisekedi “openly declares that he wants to remain in power until someone strong enough can drive him out.” The opposition has vowed to resist any change and called for elections scheduled for 2028, though a researcher noted it is difficult to envision holding them given the security context. Former president Joseph Kabila’s armed movement threatens force against what they call tyranny.
items.title: DRC Opposition Vows Resistance to Tshisekedi Constitutional Changes

items.summary: Reuters reports that Northwestern Polytechnical University bought two H200 chips for 874,700 yuan ($123,000), per an October 21 procurement record. The university is on the US Commerce Department's Entity List since 2001, with export restrictions tightened in 2019. Records show it also rented servers containing H200 chips through domestic suppliers this year. Reuters reviews found other Chinese universities buying restricted Nvidia chips or renting computing services using them. Northwestern Polytechnical, Nvidia and the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security did not respond to comment requests.
items.title: Nvidia Chips Reach Military-Linked Chinese University

items.summary: Jensen Huang admitted an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. Nvidia supplies over 80% of high-end AI chips (quantity-1007-1010), restricting sales to China since 2022 (date-1684-1688). After the disclosure, its share price fell as analysts question whether it ignored sanctions. Reports claim an Nvidia executive pressured US officials regarding Megaspeed, and the company faces a criminal investigation while Congress requests Huang explain his interactions with Alice Huang. Sales restrictions may stall Nvidia’s pipeline if chips cannot reach China.
items.title: Nvidia’s AI Dominance and Jensen Huang Scandal

items.summary: The RBI issued new domestic money transfer directions on November 11, 2026 (date-546-563), effective immediately. They cover cash-based remittances for people without bank accounts and set limits: Rs 10,000 per transaction with a monthly cap of Rs 25,000 per beneficiary (quantity-737-747; quantity-816-822), up to Rs 50,000 via NEFT by walk-in customers (quantity-1574-1580), and Rs 5,000 per transaction with a monthly cap of Rs 25,000 for ATM and business correspondent transfers (quantity-1937-1942; quantity-1984-1990). The rules apply to scheduled commercial banks, Regional Rural Banks (entity-3897-3923), entity-3935-3962) and authorised payment system operators (entity-4057-4116).
items.title: RBI Issues Domestic Money Transfer Rules

items.summary: Miguel Bezos fled Cuba at 16 under Operation Pedro Pan and rebuilt a career in engineering. In February 1995 he personally invested $100,000 in his son Jeff's online bookstore; a later contribution of $145,500 brought their combined total to approximately $245,500, commonly rounded to $250,000. Jeff recalled warning them there was a 70% chance they could lose everything. Based on Amazon's stock splits and an illustrative share price of $266.93, the holding is hypothetically worth approximately $91.63 billion, exceeding Panama's 2025 GDP of about $90.46 billion.
items.title: Jeff Bezos' Father Invested $250,000 in Amazon

items.summary: Reuters reports Nvidia's board is considering the future of CEO Jensen Huang amid speculation about his departure. Analysts point to CFO Colette Kress for an interim role and engineer Ian Buck as a long-term candidate, while external names like Arm CEO Rene Haas are also discussed. The succession debate follows allegations involving Huang, whom he acknowledged in a letter on Sunday. Nvidia shares lost around $430 billion over Monday and Tuesday, falling 9.5%, before recovering 2.9% Wednesday then dropping more than 8% after-hours.
items.title: CFO Colette Kress to engineer Ian Buck - who could succeed Nvidia CEO if he exits?

items.summary: The Free Press Journal’s noon digest reports Nvidia directors reportedly weighed ousting CEO Jensen Huang amid claims involving executive Kimberly Powell and businesswoman Alice Huang. His daughter Madison, son Spencer and son-in-law Nico Caprez work at the chipmaker; none has been named successor. The item also lists other headlines: two missing SPOs found shot dead in J&K’s Kishtwar district on Thursday, Meta infrastructure chief Santosh Janardhan to step down by early 2027 after 15 years.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Faces Possible Ouster Amid Affair Allegations

items.summary: Hindustan Times published a morning news briefing on November 12 covering several developments, including reports that Nvidia's board is working with an outside firm to identify Jensen Huang's replacement amid claims of multiple affairs. The brief also reported Iran set seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Punjab Kings acquired Hardik Pandya in an IPL trade worth Rs1.65 crore pay hike, and Anirudh Ravichander married Kavya Maran reportedly in Greece.
items.title: HT Morning Brief Covers Nvidia CEO Scandal and IPL Trade

items.summary: A controversy has erupted at Delhi University's Ramanujan College over allegations that a student linked to the National Students' Union of India approached female freshers on WhatsApp groups, offering cash incentives between 10,000 and 30,000 rupees plus flight tickets and VIP passes for male companionship. NSUI President Vinod Jakhar said the accused was suspended in September.
items.title: DU Diljit Concert Row: Freshers Lured on WhatsApp as NSUI Faces Heat Over Student

items.summary: A report says Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang over his extramarital affairs, including one with a Chinese spy. The Wall Street Journal said the board was set to meet on November 12 to decide his fate. Shares fell around 8 per cent in after-hours trading, and the company has lost about $600 billion in value since an investigation began. Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating, while analyst Gil Luria of DA Davidson warned removal could be challenging without a succession plan.
items.title: Nvidia Board May Remove Jensen Huang Over Affairs Report

items.summary: Nvidia shares reportedly declined more than 8% in extended trading on Wednesday amid reports of uncertainty surrounding the leadership of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Jensen Huang. The chipmaker's stock fell $14.95 to $158.78, compared with its regular-session closing price of $173.73. Reports suggest possible changes at senior management and questions about executive oversight.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Fall After-Hours Amid CEO Uncertainty

items.summary: Tata Power Co. Chief Executive Officer Praveer Sinha said Wednesday the company expects to sign agreements with four Indian states, including Rajasthan and Haryana, allowing cost-reflective electricity pricing from its 4-gigawatt Gujarat plant. The company reported net income of ₹1,370 crore ($146 million) for July-September, up 49 per cent year over year.
items.title: Tata Power Seeks State Tariff Deals for Mundra Plant

items.summary: Jensen Huang of Nvidia admitted an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. The scandal has drawn scrutiny because Nvidia supplies the high-end chips central to artificial intelligence and data centres. Sales of its most powerful chips to China have been restricted since 2022, though relaxed last year. Southeast Asian firms including Megaspeed are accused of exporting banned chips into China; trade records indicate over $3 billion in chips crossed from Singapore to China in a single year. Nvidia’s share price has fallen after the disclosure, and the company is reportedly under criminal investigation while Congress requests explanations.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Threatens AI Chip Giant Amid China Ties

items.summary: Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal and his daughter Harshita reportedly received a death threat from someone claiming membership in jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi's gang, demanding Rs 7 crore. The sender allegedly threatened to kill them if the demand was not met. Tilak Nagar MLA Jarnail Singh filed a complaint with Mohali Police on November 6; police registered a case and assigned Inspector Sunil Kumar.
items.title: Kejriwal Family Faces Death Threats Over Extortion Demand

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday recalled how a group of journalists told him he had become chief minister of Gujarat, jokingly asking him to distribute sweets. Speaking at the BJP's Diwali Milan event for journalists in New Delhi, PM Modi said only a few senior party leaders knew about the development when reporters entered his room and announced it.
items.title: Modi recalls journalists breaking news of his Gujarat CM role

items.summary: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng Svendsen alleged that the Indian embassy in Oslo stopped her from travelling to a Congress-organised summit in Hyderabad, cancelling her visa 10 minutes before she left for the airport. She said “orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa,” suggesting political motivation tied to her May questioning of Narendra Modi and criticism of Adani and Ambani. The home ministry, external affairs ministry and embassy had not commented. About 200 international delegates attended; clearance was obtained for 316 foreign delegates.
items.title: Norwegian Journalist Alleges India Cancelled Her Visa

items.summary: Cupid reported September-quarter revenue from operations of Rs 188 crore, up 122% year-on-year, with net profit reaching Rs 56 crore against Rs 24 crore a year earlier. The company raised FY27-FY29 guidance for higher revenue and profitability. Shares rose about 577% over the past year, valuing at around Rs 48,407 crore market capitalisation.
items.title: Cupid Shares Rally on Strong Q2 Profit and Raised Guidance

items.summary: Ola Electric shares rose to Rs 37 apiece, noted as only the second time in a month the stock crossed this level. The sharp 9% surge over two days added more than Rs 1,400 crore to market capitalisation, pushing it above Rs 17,150 crore. The rise follows the Finance Ministry making EVs the default and preferred choice for government staff car procurement, doubling the net dealer price ceiling to Rs 20 lakh while ICE vehicles are fixed at Rs 10 lakh.
items.title: Ola Electric Shares Rise on EV Procurement Policy

items.summary: The Union government reduced India's visa categories from 13 to 9 and sub-categories from 23 to 49, per the Ministry of Home Affairs (quantity-82-83, quantity-89-91, quantity-114-116). Application-form fields were cut by roughly two-thirds. The changes aim to ease travel for tourism, medical treatment, education and business, with visas expected by end of 2026.
items.title: India Cuts Visa Categories and Simplifies Application Forms

items.summary: Veeraswamy, the UK’s oldest Indian restaurant on London’s Regent Street and a venue that served Churchill, Chaplin and Brando, faces closure after The Crown Estate declined to renew its lease at Victory House for renovation work. Owner Ranjit Mathrani says the business is being treated unfairly; the landlord rejects this claim. The dispute now proceeds under the Landlord and Tenant Act, with court proceedings begun on November 5 determining whether Veeraswamy can keep its lease.
items.title: Veeraswamy restaurant forced to close as Crown Estate declines lease renewal

items.summary: Former Uttarakhand Chief Minister Harish Rawat said he will not seek the chief minister’s post or any other office if Congress wins a majority in the 2027 Assembly elections, according to Press Trust of India. His stated goal is helping Congress form the state government and ousting the BJP.
items.title: Harish Rawat Rules Out CM Bid

items.summary: A fire swept through Parsi Parlo town in Arunachal Pradesh’s Kurung Kumey district early Thursday morning, killing at least four people including three children and a woman. Police sources said the blaze broke out around 2am and was suspected to have originated in a kitchen, though its exact cause remains under investigation. The tragedy exposed the lack of firefighting infrastructure in the remote area.
items.title: Fire Kills Four in Arunachal’s Kurung Kumey

items.summary: An article argues that India is working to revive its Vishwaguru image through a limited role in the ongoing peace talks, which are being brokered by the US. New Delhi stays off the negotiation table but focuses on protecting Indian seafarers and maintaining grain supplies for the Global South. Kanwal Sibal says these reflect two immediate concerns: the welfare of Indian seafarers and commercial shipping safety. Ambassador Anil Wadhwa notes that India's shift toward concrete proposals reflects greater diplomatic confidence, though he warns against overstating its capacity to broker a final settlement.
items.title: India's Modest Role in Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks

items.summary: Chief Minister V D Satheesan said ensuring quality fuel is non-negotiable and oil companies' interests cannot take priority over people's welfare. The government directed the Civil Supplies Department to intensify petrol pump inspections, with nine samples collected on November 9 from Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Kannur districts. Results are expected within ten days, and violations will invite legal action.
items.title: Kerala CM Prioritises Consumer Fuel Quality Over Oil Firms

items.summary: Kia India will invest USD 2 billion to build a new manufacturing facility in Andhra Pradesh, per Gwanggu Lee, Managing Director and CEO of Kia India. The project is expected to create around 12,000 jobs and raise annual production capacity to more than 6 lakh units.
items.title: Kia India Announces USD 2 Billion Investment in Andhra Pradesh
